mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% annualized over the previous month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points over the previous month signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances when UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the previous two months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances when HOUST increases over two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous two months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face reduced output and potential earnings declines.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances when INDPRO decreases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% year-over-year, it signals a tightening monetary policy coupled with slowing economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: tightening monetary policy with slowing growth
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances when FEDFUNDS is above 4% and GDPC1 YoY growth is below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the previous month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.1 percentage points, signals a robust labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances when PAYEMS increases by more than 200k and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.1pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the previous two months signals strengthening consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances when RSAFS increases over two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) decreases by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous month, it signals a loosening monetary policy, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate increased liquidity and lower borrowing costs.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS decreases by more than 0.5pp.
